  - region "Simple English explanation of Line Through Two Points in 3D":

      - heading "Understand Line Through Two Points in 3D" [level=2]
  - text: CLASS 12 • THREE-DIMENSIONAL GEOMETRY
  - heading "Line Through Two Points in 3D" [level=1]
  - paragraph: Build the vector and parametric equations of a line from two points and trace any point on it.
  - text: 18 min ADVANCED CONCEPT geometry3d
  - main:
    - text: INTERACTIVE LAB
    - 'heading "Line Explorer: Two-Point Construction" [level=2]'
    - paragraph: Drag points A and B, move the slider t, and explore the line through them in 3D.
    - complementary:
      - button "Reset lab":
        - img
        - text: Reset lab
      - text: Show axes
      - checkbox "Show axes" [checked]
    - article:
      - text: 3D CONSTRUCTION
      - paragraph: Drag A or B to update the line.
      - navigation:
        - button "Select points":
          - img
        - button "Rotate view":
          - img
        - button "Pan view":
          - img
        - button "Zoom view":
          - img
        - button "Fit view":
          - img
      - img "Draggable line through two points in 3D": A (1, 2, 3) B (4, 6, 5) P (7, 10, 7)
      - text: Parameter t
      - slider "Line parameter t": "2"
      - status: t = 2.00
      - paragraph:
        - text: Point on line P = A + td
        - strong: P (7, 10, 7)
    - complementary:
      - heading "FROM POINTS TO LINE" [level=3]
      - article:
        - text: Point A
        - strong: A (1, 2, 3)
        - text: x
        - spinbutton "Point A x": "1"
        - text: "y"
        - spinbutton "Point A y": "2"
        - text: z
        - spinbutton "Point A z": "3"
      - article:
        - text: Point B
        - strong: B (4, 6, 5)
        - text: x
        - spinbutton "Point B x": "4"
        - text: "y"
        - spinbutton "Point B y": "6"
        - text: z
        - spinbutton "Point B z": "5"
      - article:
        - text: Direction vector d = B − A
        - strong: d = (3, 4, 2)
      - article:
        - text: Line (Vector Form)
        - paragraph: r = (1, 2, 3) + t (3, 4, 2)
      - article:
        - text: Parametric Equations
        - paragraph: x = 1 + 3t y = 2 + 4t z = 3 + 2t
    - article:
      - heading "COMPONENT DIFFERENCE VISUAL" [level=3]
      - text: B − A = d
      - img: A (1,2,3) B (4,6,5) d = (3,4,2)
    - article:
      - heading "COLLINEARITY VERIFICATION" [level=3]
      - paragraph: For any t, vector AP is a scalar multiple of d.
      - paragraph: AP = P − A = (6, 8, 4)
      - paragraph: td = 2(3, 4, 2) = (6, 8, 4)
      - strong:
        - img
        - text: AP = td ✓ Collinear
    - article:
      - heading "DIRECTION MATTERS, LINE DOES NOT" [level=3]
      - paragraph: Reversing the points changes the direction vector but not the line.
      - paragraph: "Original: A → B d = (3,4,2)"
      - paragraph: "Reversed: B → A d′ = (-3,-4,-2)"
      - text: Both equations represent the same geometric line.
    - article:
      - heading "QUICK CHECKS" [level=3]
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: "|d| = √(3²+4²+2²) = 5.39"
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: "Angle with x-axis: 56.15°"
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: "Angle with y-axis: 42.03°"
      - paragraph:
        - img
        - text: "Angle with z-axis: 68.20°"
    - heading "WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=3]
    - paragraph: Find the line through C(2,-1,4) and D(5,3,10), and the point at t=-1.
    - article:
      - text: "Step 1: Direction vector"
      - paragraph: d=D−C=(3,4,6)
    - article:
      - text: "Step 2: Vector equation"
      - paragraph: r=(2,-1,4)+t(3,4,6)
    - article:
      - text: "Step 3: Parametric equations"
      - paragraph: x=2+3t y=-1+4t z=4+6t
    - article:
      - text: "Step 4: Point at t=-1"
      - paragraph: P=(-1,-5,-2)
    - heading "PRACTICE" [level=3]
    - paragraph: For each pair, find d, the vector equation, parametric equations, and P at t=2.
    - article:
      - text: 1 A(0,1,2), B(2,5,-1)
      - group: Show result
    - article:
      - text: 2 A(-3,2,1), B(1,6,7)
      - group: Show result
    - article:
      - text: 3 A(4,-2,3), B(-2,2,11)
      - group: Show result
